proof:
Source. Step 5 of the parent proof of Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 (chapter-03.txt lines 25–66; the 'only if' part is lines 39–65).
- The printed proof says: if the Jacobian of G_{ij} is non-zero at x, then for some ρ > 0 the set G_{ij}(B_ρ(x)) is an n-dimensional C¹ submanifold of ℝ^{n+ℓ}, with G_{ij} as a local representation. (Erratum: the book prints ℝ^n.)
- The parent proof records the quantitative content of this inverse-function argument as a lower Lipschitz bound on a ball. That bound is the present statement, for a single C¹ map G.
- A non-zero Jacobian J_G(x) = √det(DG(x)* DG(x)) means exactly that DG(x) is injective.
Notation: |·| is the Euclidean norm, ‖A‖ the operator norm of a linear map A, and B_δ(x) the open ball.

1. (Coercivity of L.) Put L := DG(x), an injective linear map ℝ^n → ℝ^P.
- Since ℝ^n is finite-dimensional, L is a linear isomorphism of ℝ^n onto the subspace L(ℝ^n). Its inverse L(ℝ^n) → ℝ^n is linear on a finite-dimensional normed space, hence bounded.
- So there is N > 0 with |v| ≤ N|Lv| for every v ∈ ℝ^n. (Equivalently: if n ≥ 1, v ↦ |Lv| is continuous and positive on the compact unit sphere, so it has a positive minimum. If n = 0, every v is 0 and any N > 0 works.)
- Put μ := 1/(2N) > 0. Then |Lv| ≥ |v|/N = 2μ|v| for all v ∈ ℝ^n.
2. (Continuity of DG at x.) G is C¹, so y ↦ DG(y) is continuous from ℝ^n into the linear maps ℝ^n → ℝ^P with the operator norm, in particular at x. Choose δ > 0 with ‖DG(y) − L‖ ≤ μ for all y ∈ B_δ(x).
3. (Mean value inequality.) Let φ(y) := G(y) − L(y).
- Since L is linear, φ is differentiable at every y with Dφ(y) = DG(y) − L. So ‖Dφ(y)‖ ≤ μ for y ∈ B_δ(x).
- The ball B_δ(x) is convex, so the mean value inequality gives |φ(a) − φ(b)| ≤ μ|a − b| for all a, b ∈ B_δ(x).
- Since L is linear, φ(a) − φ(b) = G(a) − G(b) − L(a − b). Hence |G(a) − G(b) − L(a − b)| ≤ μ|a − b|.
4. (Conclusion.) Let a, b ∈ B_δ(x). By the triangle inequality and steps 1 and 3,
 |G(a) − G(b)| ≥ |L(a − b)| − |G(a) − G(b) − L(a − b)| ≥ 2μ|a − b| − μ|a − b| = μ|a − b|.
So δ > 0 and μ > 0 have the required property. ∎

Implementation note (not part of the mathematics). No extra import is needed.
- Step 1: apply LinearMap.injective_iff_antilipschitz to (fderiv ℝ G x : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P). This gives N > 0 with AntilipschitzWith N. ZeroHomClass.bound_of_antilipschitz then gives ‖v‖ ≤ N * ‖L v‖.
- Steps 2–3 together say that G approximates L with constant μ near x, which is strict differentiability:
  - hG.contDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt (by norm_num) : HasStrictFDerivAt G (fderiv ℝ G x) x.
  - HasStrictFDerivAt.approximates_deriv_on_nhds with c := ⟨μ, hμ.le⟩ gives s ∈ 𝓝 x with ApproximatesLinearOn G L s c. This means ‖G a - G b - L (a - b)‖ ≤ μ * ‖a - b‖ for a, b ∈ s; apply it as happrox a ha b hb.
  - Metric.mem_nhds_iff gives δ > 0 with ball x δ ⊆ s.
  - Alternatively, use Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le directly for step 3.
- Step 4: norm_sub_le, then nlinarith.
